recommendation: Repair chapter 16 in one coordinated change set spanning the canon chapter, the equipment summary and the reference sheet, then re-verify before publication. Concretely: keep the defect bounded to the two strictly dominated armour rows, Studded Leather and Half Plate, and rebuild the table so every surviving row carries one consistent price per DR step and one consistent price for the shared Stealth Bane and speed cut; re-sweep all eight rows on every printed axis and report zero new strictly dominated pairs; never price or condemn a body-armour row against a build that carries a shield. Restate the spellcasting penalties on the callout as the prose Bane counts the table above it already prints (Plate a Triple Bane, Breastplate a single Bane), with no numeric Bane translation anywhere, and reconcile the Breastplate's promotion as a caster's armour with the Bane its own row carries. Rebuild both worked examples from the class kit's DR 7 baseline, charge the shield exactly once (in coin or in rank, not both), and ship the coupled example's corrected derived figures in the same change. Align the weight classes so the class carrying the five-foot cut is exactly the class the chapter calls heavy, state the suit-up-time consequence for the relocated rows where the class is stated, and publish the class as a row-level marker mirrored in every restatement of the armour table plus a glossary headword. State the shield prerequisite exemption for shields rather than for kit weapons alone, reconcile the duplicate prerequisite names and the glossary collision to one term, and correct or restate the Shield Block rule where its description and its arithmetic diverge. Justify the table's column budget by the binding header string of each shrunk column and report the clearance margin against the alternative split. Do not reopen the monster-DR comparisons as cross-chapter defects.
rationale: t-01: the convention audit established a real but bounded defect - exactly two armour rows are strictly dominated - while the offered three-cell remedy failed its own arithmetic test and reached only one of the three files that print the changed value, so the repair is legal only under r-001's conditions (mirror every changed value in every printing file, one consistent price per DR step and for the shared drawback, zero new dominated pairs on a full re-sweep, no shield-armed comparison, header-justified column widths). t-02: the procedure audit found the chapter's prose and its stat rows pointing opposite ways at the same three points; r-002 keeps the tables' register, so the callout's numeric penalties become the Bane counts printed above them, the Plate-domination claim falls because it armed one side with a shield, and both worked examples must be rebuilt from the kit's DR 7 baseline with the shield charged once and the coupled example moved with them. t-03: the canon audit cleared every printed gear value and all three shields across the chapters while finding the weight-class vocabulary unlookupable even though it carries rule weight outside this chapter; r-003 therefore orders publication rather than surgery - a row-level class marker mirrored in every restatement plus a glossary headword - confirms the kit-baseline example and the shield exemption, and closes the monster-DR lead for good. The conditions of r-002 and r-003 converge on the same cells the r-001 repair touches, which is why the chapter must be fixed in one pass rather than by chapter-local patches; every outcome below is stated inside those three rulings and none of them reopens a sealed point.

resolved.outcome: Convention conformance fails on a bounded defect: exactly two armour rows, Studded Leather and Half Plate, are strictly dominated, and no other row may be called dominated against a shield-carrying build. The repair may not be sealed as scoped to the canon chapter alone nor on the arithmetic as offered - every value it changes must be changed in every chapter that prints that value, the repaired table must carry one consistent price per DR step and one consistent price for the shared drawback, and the eight-row re-sweep must report zero new dominated pairs. The column-budget change stands on its confirmed effect, that the table closes on one printed page with all eight rows, but the chosen widths must be justified by the binding header of each shrunk column rather than by the longest cell value, with the clearance margin reported against the alternative split (r-001).

Internal procedure consistency is repaired in the tables' register, since both registers are operative: the spellcasting callout's numeric penalties are replaced by the Bane counts its own table prints (Plate a Triple Bane, Breastplate a single Bane) and no numeric Bane translation may replace them, with the Breastplate's recommendation allowed to stand only at the cost its own row carries. The dominated-row finding stands for the two duplicate-DR rows; the further claim that Plate is dominated is not established and is dropped. Both worked examples are rebuilt from the class kit's DR 7 baseline with the shield charged exactly once and consistently, the coupled second example's derived figures corrected in the same change, the weight classes assigned so the class carrying the five-foot cut is exactly the class the chapter calls heavy with the suit-up-time consequence accepted and stated, and the Shield Block rule corrected or restated where its description and its arithmetic diverge (r-002).

Cross-chapter canon is not clean but narrowly so: the gear values and all three shields agree row for row across the chapters that print them and may not be revised on consistency grounds alone, while two contradictions stand and must be repaired. The class carrying the five-foot speed cut and the class the book calls heavy are made the same set, and because that class carries rule weight outside this chapter while being registered nowhere a reader can look, the class is published rather than cut - a row-level class marker mirrored in every restatement of the armour table plus a glossary headword, each closing a different half of the gap - with the worked example totalling from the class kit and the shield prerequisite exemption stated for shields rather than kit weapons alone. The monster-DR lead is withdrawn and must not be revived as a defect (r-003).

dissent.position: The three-cell repair cannot be sealed as scoped to the canon chapter: the DR value it moves is printed in the canon home, in the equipment summary and on the reference sheet, so the real edit set is five cells across three files, and a literally executed canon-chapter-only edit would make the canon home read DR 3 while the two restatements still read 2. Its ladder also fails its own rate: the repriced DR-4 row sits 15 gp under the next rung at identical requirement, identical Bane and identical speed cut, so pricing the untouched quiet row at the repair's own rate puts the breastplate at 40 gp and reinstates the very DR-4 domination the repair removed - zero new dominated pairs holds only at the one number the fix did not touch. The same incoherence runs on the drawback side, where the identical Stealth Bane is discounted on the DR-3 pair and charged, bundled with the speed cut, on the DR-4 pair. The column split survives its test but not its stated basis: it is justified by the longest entry a column holds when the string the shrink must actually fit is that column's header, and splitting the same budget evenly between the two binding headers is cheaper at no cost to the total.

Plate is the table's worst case and is dominated: the chapter's own Option B reaches the identical DR 6 for 115 gp with no Stealth Bane, no speed cut, one fewer Armor rank needed and an extra reaction, so Plate's 300 gp is a 185 gp surplus at 2.61x that build, and its last DR point costs 225 gp against a prior step of 50 gp. Recorded as a minority position that does not survive the ruling: the council held the claim not established because the comparison arms one side with a shield while the other has none, and a shield stacks with every body-armour row.

The monster-DR lead as first filed, at lower confidence: the bestiary names armour in its monster-DR parentheticals, and the tie with this chapter's values holds for the Orc Warchief's plate but breaks for a hobgoblin chain shirt printed at DR 1 against this chapter's 3. The lead was then withdrawn on the record - monster DR tracks the bestiary's Challenge budget (halve, round down, cap at six, then hand-tune), the armour name is a descriptive label rather than the source of the number, and the only alignment is the shared ceiling of six. Preserved as a recorded minority position; r-003 closed it and it may not be revived as a cross-chapter defect.
